recovery_title: Where you look matters: visual cortex hurts, somatomotor helps
recovery_takeaway: Visual cortex recovers 0.125 worse than random vertices of the same count; somatomotor 0.102 better, beating the whole cortex at the same budget (0.851 vs 0.836). Both effects are ~10× the control seed spread (≤ 0.013). Left language +0.023; homologue, auditory, default mode within noise.
recovery_notes: Each network is inverted observing only its own vertices; each has a random control of identical size (same seeding scheme as the extent sweep), and two networks have a second random seed: language controls differ by 0.0014, auditory controls by 0.0126, which bounds control variability. Whole-cortex anchor reproduces the earlier GPU value exactly (0.8362), so the CPU run is comparable. All values at a fixed 8 000-step budget and one ground truth: we claim relative differences within this run, not converged absolute values. Auditory is low in absolute terms simply because it has only 277 vertices (cf. extent curve).
slots_title: The regional effect is not modality-specific
slots_body: Split recovery into the text-, audio- and video-derived thirds of x. If a network helped only with the modality it encodes, visual cortex would recover video dimensions well. Instead, every network shifts all three thirds together: visual cortex loses text, audio and video alike; somatomotor gains all three.
slots_takeaway: Regional recoverability is a property of how a region's response is shaped, not of which modality it is tuned to.
slots_notes: Contrast with the topography slide: visual cortex is the most video-dominated network (z = +40.7), yet recovering the video-derived dimensions from visual cortex is worse than from random vertices (−0.116). Predictable is not the same as recoverable, even within a region's preferred modality.
pvr_body:
Visual cortex responds most strongly to the representation (1.60× cortex mean) and is the worst place to decode it from. Somatomotor responds least (0.73×) and is the best.

Partial mechanism: response diversity. Somatomotor's response spans the most independent directions (participation ratio 18.6 vs 15.2 matched; top direction carries 15% of variance). Visual responses are strong but concentrated (PR 10.3; top direction 27%).

Language and auditory are also concentrated yet near their controls, so diversity explains the extremes, not every network. Six networks are too few for a correlation claim.
pvr_notes: Participation ratio = (sum of squared singular values)^2 / sum of fourth powers, of the ROI's response matrix to 128 random input directions: the number of independent input directions the region can tell apart. Practical implication worth stating: a uniform whole-cortex MSE is dominated by high-gain, low-diversity regions such as visual cortex; this predicts that down-weighting them could improve whole-cortex decoding. That is a testable next step, not a result. Caveat: at a fixed 8 000-step budget we cannot separate 'better optimum' from 'faster convergence' for somatomotor.
synthesis_where: Strong responses are not the best evidence: visual cortex decodes worst, somatomotor best (−0.125 / +0.102 vs matched).
